checks.invariant: GET /cameras and GET /cameras/{id} return only cameras inside the caller's role scope (resident: c.user_id = self; community_admin: same community AND common, own, or admin_can_view)
checks.result: list_cameras (cameras.py:78-83) and get_camera (cameras.py:86-95) both apply _scope (cameras.py:69-75). Every value is parameterized, and the identity comes only from the session user returned by auth.current_user; no request field overrides it. The admin predicate binds c.community_id to the session community_id. get_camera rejects anything that is not a UUID. A missing camera and an out-of-scope camera get the same 404 (_camera_not_found, app.py:695-698). No path returns a camera outside the scope.

checks.invariant: Only the owner of a private camera can change admin_can_view (POST /cameras/{id}/visibilidad)
checks.result: set_admin_visibility (cameras.py:183-191) runs UPDATE ... WHERE id = %s AND user_id = <session user> AND kind = 'private' RETURNING id. A non-owner, a common camera or a non-UUID updates no rows, and the route answers 404 (app.py:737-741). The redirect target is the UUID that was already validated. Nothing else in app.py or manage.py writes admin_can_view. CSRF on this POST is h1's coverage.

checks.invariant: The camera detail page shows only events and aggregates the caller may see, and the camera scope (_scope) agrees with the event scope (list_events) for each role
checks.result: camera_page (app.py:715-734) calls get_camera first, then list_events(user, camera_id=cam['id']), which applies the role predicate again (app.py:281-286). The count subqueries in cameras._SELECT (cameras.py:59-64) count only events of a camera that already passed the scope check. A resident's camera can only receive events from its owner (resolve_camera, cameras.py:149-162) or from its assigned edge device. The one difference: _scope admits an admin through c.kind = 'common', while list_events and the evidence query admit through c.admin_can_view. Common cameras are created with admin_can_view = true (schema default at schema_vigia.sql:138), and set_admin_visibility only changes private cameras, so this difference can only hide events, never expose them. The admin audit entry for viewing someone else's private camera is written (app.py:726-731).

checks.invariant: The composite (id, community_id) foreign keys make the id-only LEFT JOINs (events->cameras, media_files->cameras) community-consistent, and no camera, user or community can be reassigned
checks.result: cameras (user_id, community_id) -> users and (edge_device_id, community_id) -> edge_devices (schema_vigia.sql:145-148). events (user_id|camera_id, community_id) (schema_vigia.sql:169-172). media_files (user_id|camera_id|event_id, community_id) (schema_vigia.sql:192-197). Under MATCH SIMPLE a key with a NULL column is not checked, but any non-NULL camera_id must belong to the row's own community. Neither the app nor manage.py has an UPDATE that changes cameras.user_id, kind or community_id, or users.community_id, and neither deletes cameras or users. So the joins the scoping queries trust cannot cross a community.

checks.invariant: Camera creation binds community and owner to the session, not to request fields
checks.result: create_camera (cameras.py:108-125) takes community_id and user_id from the session user, always sets kind = 'private', and validates name and place with text_issue. default_camera (cameras.py:128-146) is the same. The form supplies only name and place. Two side effects are non-findings, recorded under hardening: the per-community unique-name message, and the count-then-insert quota check.

checks.invariant: Resident event listing (GET /, GET /events) returns only events the resident created or events on cameras the resident owns
checks.result: The resident predicate is (e.user_id = self OR c.user_id = self) (app.py:285-286). events.user_id is set only from the session user in insert_event (app.py:226-227). camera_id comes from resolve_camera (owner, private, active; cameras.py:149-162) for /ws/live and /analyze, or from edge_camera for /ingest. A resident therefore cannot cause another person's event to match, and cannot see one.

checks.invariant: Admin event listing is bound to the admin's community and excludes private cameras hidden by their owner
checks.result: The admin predicate is e.community_id = <session community> AND (c.id IS NULL OR c.admin_can_view OR c.user_id = self) (app.py:282-283). The composite FK (schema_vigia.sql:171-172) forces the camera into the same community. Cameraless events are visible by design (edge events without a camera). The current code never creates user-owned cameraless events: /ws/live and /analyze always pass camera_id (app.py:533, app.py:608). Rows written before commit 5999fbf were inserted without camera_id (git show 5999fbf) and remain visible to the admin; that is unchanged from the previous policy and recorded under hardening.

checks.invariant: Derived fields in the event projection (reasons, image, owner_name, camera_name) disclose nothing beyond the in-scope event
checks.result: The reasons column is string_agg over the fixed signals.description catalog (app.py:259-261, schema_vigia.sql:208-216). Free-text /ingest reasons only map to codes in parse_reasons (app.py:205-218), and event_signals.detail is never selected. The image subquery returns only media rows of the same in-scope event (app.py:262-264). owner_name and camera_name come from the joined camera or user of an in-scope event, and owner_name is rendered on the home page only for admins (app.py:750). Dashboard and JSON responses are no-store (app.py:156).

checks.invariant: List filters and limits give no enumeration or aggregate oracle across scope
checks.result: /events accepts only limit, cast to int and clamped to 1..500 (app.py:280, app.py:648-650). Camera filters run only after get_camera succeeds. nivel is whitelisted (app.py:721). Dates are parsed with date.fromisoformat (app.py:688-692). limite must be ASCII digits and is clamped to 12..200 (app.py:724). No filter can count or test events outside the role predicate.

checks.invariant: The per-role evidence predicate is equivalent to the event-list predicate
checks.result: The evidence admin branch (app.py:660-665) and resident branch (app.py:666-670) mirror list_events (app.py:281-286), joined on media_files.camera_id. insert_event writes the same community_id, user_id and camera_id to the event and to its media row (app.py:230-249). The composite FKs (schema_vigia.sql:192-197) keep the media community consistent with its camera and event. No predicate disagreement between /evidence and the listing.

checks.invariant: The file served by /evidence/{name} was produced for the principal that owns the authorizing media_files row
checks.result: Not enforced. storage_key is globally UNIQUE with no tenant component (schema_vigia.sql:186). The first insert wins and later ones are dropped by ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING (app.py:248). /evidence checks only the row and os.path.exists before FileResponse on a flat shared EVIDENCE_DIR (app.py:30, 672-683). Video evidence names are deterministic, evt_{sanitized upload filename}_{video-time ms}.jpg (engine.py:87-88), so a later upload by a different user or community writes its frame over the earlier claimant's file (engine.py:95). The detector also writes into the same directory (notifier.py:22-28, main.py:141, docker-compose.yml:20/38). sha256 is never populated (schema_vigia.sql:189). Proposed as needs_validation: backend/app.py:evidence:first-claimant-storage-key-serves-shared-evidence-file.

checks.invariant: The evidence name cannot leave EVIDENCE_DIR
checks.result: IMAGE_NAME_RE ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,120}$ (app.py:71, app.py:656) forbids path separators. Only '.' and '..' resolve to directories, and they also need a media row; FileResponse on a directory fails rather than reading a file. No file outside EVIDENCE_DIR is reachable.

checks.invariant: Admin reads of another person's evidence are audited
checks.result: An audit row is inserted when an admin reads a media row whose user_id is not the admin's (app.py:675-682). For edge media on a resident's private camera, media_files.user_id is NULL, so subject_user_id is NULL instead of the camera owner. This is an accuracy gap, not an access bypass, and is recorded under hardening.

checks.invariant: fill() substitutes placeholders in a single pass and never re-interprets inserted values
checks.result: pages.fill (pages.py:21-27) is re.sub over the template, with an alternation of re.escape'd keys and a callable replacement. The callable's return value is inserted literally, with no backreference expansion, and is not scanned again. A value containing '{cards}' or '{nonce}' therefore stays literal. Placeholders appear only at index.html:295/319/387/396, camara.html:9-300, camaras.html:264-309 and login.html:236/243. None sits inside a script body except the nonce attribute, which gets secrets.token_urlsafe.

checks.invariant: Every stored or user-supplied value rendered server-side is HTML-escaped for its context (text, quoted attribute, title RCDATA, href)
checks.result: These values go through html.escape or esc with quote=True: camera name and place, owner/full name, level, reasons, source label, image name in the img src (app.py:752-766, app.py:776-780; pages.py:43, 52-53, 58, 77-89, 94, 102, 107-115, 159-188, 202, 207-210), the login identifier and message (app.py:418-422), and the camera form echo (pages.py:137). Unescaped interpolations are only integers (score, counts), floats (video_time_s), DB to_char timestamps, code constants, UUIDs, and urlencode output, which is then escaped. Camera names and places are restricted by text_issue (cameras.py:35-42). The /ingest free-text reasons (≤500 chars) are never rendered; only signals.description is shown. Evidence image names are limited to [A-Za-z0-9._-]. No stored-XSS path was found.

checks.invariant: The client re-injection of the server's #eventos HTML (innerHTML) cannot turn escaped data into markup or script
checks.result: actualizarEventos (index.html:640-651) fetches same-origin '/', parses it with DOMParser, and assigns nuevo.innerHTML to contenedorEventos.innerHTML. The server markup holds only div, span and img elements. Attacker-influenced data appears only as escaped text nodes, or as attribute values limited to [A-Za-z0-9._-]. There are no raw-text, template or SVG/MathML elements, so serializing and re-parsing gives the same DOM and no mutation-XSS vector exists. CSP script-src allows only the nonce, without unsafe-inline (app.py:114-128), which would also block injected handlers. Other client sinks use textContent, className or alt. The innerHTML assignments at index.html:470 and index.html:613 are constant strings. login.html, camara.html and camaras.html contain no scripts.

checks.invariant: SQL in list_events, cameras._SELECT/_scope, /evidence and the audit inserts is fully parameterized
checks.result: Dynamic SQL is assembled only from constant fragments: _EVENTS_SELECT plus the condiciones literals (app.py:281-299), and _SELECT plus the _scope literals (cameras.py:69-95). Every value (ids, community, level, desde/hasta as datetime.date, limit/limite as clamped int) is passed through %s parameters to psycopg2. No string-formatted user data reaches cur.execute.

candidates.title: /evidence serves any file at a claimed name, so another user's or community's frame written under that name reaches the first claimant
candidates.description:
GET /evidence/{name} grants access when the caller is in scope for the single media_files row with storage_key = name. It then streams whatever file currently sits at events/<name>, a flat directory shared by every user's uploads, live sessions and the live detector. storage_key is globally unique and has no tenant part, and the first insert wins (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING). Evidence from uploaded videos is named only from the sanitized upload filename and the video-relative time (evt_<file>_<ms>.jpg).

Variant 1, resident versus resident in any community. Resident A uploads a video with a chosen filename, and the /analyze response lists the evidence names A now owns. Later, resident B in any community uploads a file with the same sanitized name, and an event fires at the same video-time stamp. B's frame overwrites the file, B's media row is silently dropped, and A's GET /evidence/<name> returns B's frame. B's event shows no image.

Variant 2, reverse direction. A later uploader replaces an earlier owner's evidence image, so that owner and their admin see foreign content as their evidence.

Variant 3, edge pre-claim. The claim step is in h3-edge-files' /ingest unit; the read-side consequence is here. An edge device can register any [A-Za-z0-9._-] name with camera_id NULL. Its community admin then passes the c.id IS NULL branch and can read whatever file later appears under that name. Examples: another community's video evidence, a hidden private camera's evidence in the same community, or the detector's intruso_<YYYYmmdd_HHMMSS>.jpg, clip_<...>.mp4 and events.jsonl in the same directory.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: The /evidence authorization is tied to who first inserted a tenant-less, globally unique storage_key, not to the file actually produced for that principal. The file is then resolved by bare name in a single shared directory that several principals write to, with predictable or principal-chosen names. Nothing binds the file's producer or content to the row: media_files.sha256 is unused, paths have no per-community or per-event segment, and a write fails open on conflict.

trace.description: An authenticated resident uploads a video; the multipart filename is attacker-chosen.
label = clean_filename(video.filename) keeps the last 80 [A-Za-z0-9._-] characters of the user's filename and passes it to the engine as source_label.
Evidence name is evt_{source_label}_{int(video_time*1000):08d}.jpg. It depends only on the filename and video-relative time, so independent uploads with the same filename collide.
cv2.imwrite writes the frame to EVIDENCE_DIR/<name> and replaces any file already there, including one owned by another principal.
The media_files row uses ON CONFLICT (storage_key) DO NOTHING. The first principal to insert a name keeps ownership, and a later producer's row is silently dropped.
The resident check matches only the stored row (m.user_id = caller OR c.user_id = caller). The admin branch (line 664) also admits cameraless rows such as edge-claimed names.
The only file check is os.path.exists on the shared path. Nothing verifies who wrote the file or what it contains.
FileResponse(path) returns the current file bytes, which may be another user's or community's frame, to the row's claimant.

evidence.description: storage_key text NOT NULL UNIQUE: one global namespace across all communities and users, with no tenant or event component.
A sha256 column exists but insert_event never sets it, so file content is never bound to the row.
EVIDENCE_DIR = BASE/events is a single flat directory, commented as shared with the detector.
The detector service mounts the same ./events directory as the backend (line 20), so detector output is in the namespace /evidence serves.
The stamp is video-relative milliseconds, not wall clock or a random value. The attacker learns their own claimed names from the /analyze response, which includes events[].image.
The image subquery selects media only by event_id. When B's media insert hits the conflict, B's event shows no image while the file under that name holds B's frame.
The admin branch admits rows with no camera (c.id IS NULL), so names claimed by an edge device with camera_id NULL are readable by that edge's community admin whatever file later appears.

The /ingest image only has to match IMAGE_NAME_RE, so an edge can register names such as evt_*.jpg, intruso_*.jpg, clip_*.mp4 or events.jsonl. insert_event records a size of 0 when the file does not exist yet (app.py:241-244). This claim side belongs to h3-edge-files.

The live detector writes intruso_<YYYYmmdd_HHMMSS>.jpg (second resolution, enumerable) and appends events.jsonl (line 22) in the shared directory; main.py:141 also writes clip_<YYYYmmdd_HHMMSS>.mp4 there.

blockers: No OS-enforced sandbox, PostgreSQL instance, or YOLO model is available in this run, so no target code was executed and the end-to-end read of another principal's frame was not observed.

Whether two independent uploads with the same sanitized filename yield an evidence event at the identical millisecond stamp depends on runtime detections, video fps, and the engine-wide ThreatScorer (engine.py:46, reused by analyze_video at engine.py:83); this was not observed locally.
cv2.imwrite replacing an existing file and PostgreSQL ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING suppressing the second row are library and DB behaviours that were not exercised.

Real-world collision likelihood depends on deployment facts: how residents name uploaded files, whether the live detector profile shares ./events with the backend in production, and who custodies edge tokens.

validation_plan.local: In an isolated sandbox with a throwaway PostgreSQL 16 loaded from bd_intivision/schema_vigia.sql, create two communities X and Y, resident A in X with private camera CA, resident B in Y with private camera CB, an admin in X, and an edge device in X. Point EVIDENCE_DIR at a scratch directory. (1) Write bytes 'A' to evt_clip.mp4_00000500.jpg and call backend.app.insert_event({'level':'MEDIO','score':3,'people':1,'image':'evt_clip.mp4_00000500.jpg'}, user=A, source_kind='video', camera_id=CA). (2) Overwrite the file with bytes 'B', as engine.analyze_video's cv2.imwrite would for B's upload of a file named clip.mp4, and call insert_event(same dict, user=B, source_kind='video', camera_id=CB). (3) With FastAPI TestClient and dummy session cookies, GET /evidence/evt_clip.mp4_00000500.jpg as A: expect 200 with body 'B'. As B: expect 404. list_events(B) should show B's event with image NULL. (4) Edge variant: call insert_event({'level':'MEDIO','score':3,'people':0,'image':'intruso_20261105_221530.jpg'}, None, X, 'edge', None) before the file exists, then create the file, then GET it as X's admin: expect 200. Optionally run analyze_video twice on the same tiny synthetic clip saved under the same name to confirm identical evt_ names. Stop at the first wrong-owner byte.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner-observed, read-only checks on the production database and host. (a) SELECT e.id, e.community_id, e.user_id FROM events e WHERE e.source = 'video' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM media_files m WHERE m.event_id = e.id). Video events that lost their media row point to storage_key collisions that already happened. (b) SELECT storage_key, community_id FROM media_files WHERE user_id IS NULL AND (storage_key LIKE 'evt\_%' OR storage_key LIKE 'intruso\_%' OR storage_key LIKE 'clip\_%' OR storage_key = 'events.jsonl'). These are edge rows that claim backend or detector names. (c) Confirm whether the detector (profile live) runs on the same host and shares ./events with the backend.

hardening: POST /cameras rejects a name already used in the community with 'Ya existe una cámara con ese nombre en tu comunidad' (cameras.py:118-124). This shows a resident whether another resident's private camera name exists, including default names 'Cámara de <full name>', which goes against the stated intent at app.py:696. Probing is limited because each wrong guess creates a camera and the count check (cameras.py:115-117) stops everything after MAX_CAMERAS_PER_USER. Consider owner-scoped uniqueness or a generic error.
create_camera does a count then an insert (cameras.py:115-121) outside a lock or constraint, so concurrent POST /cameras requests can exceed MAX_CAMERAS_PER_USER. This is a quota issue only.

Browser and video events written before commit 5999fbf have camera_id NULL (the previous insert_event calls passed no camera). The admin branch (c.id IS NULL, app.py:282 and app.py:664) keeps showing them and their evidence to the community admin whatever the owner's per-camera admin_can_view choice, and they appear on no camera page. Consider backfilling camera_id. If a camera or user row were ever deleted, ON DELETE SET NULL (camera_id) (schema_vigia.sql:172, 195) would also turn edge events and media of a hidden private camera into cameraless rows the admin can see; no deletion path exists today.

Evidence audit (app.py:675-682) takes subject_user_id from media_files.user_id. That is NULL for edge events on a resident's private camera, so the camera owner is not recorded. Admin views of other residents' private-camera events on / and /events are not audited; only /cameras/{id} and /evidence are.

/evidence responses are sent with Cache-Control: private, max-age=600 (app.py:156). Images can stay in the browser cache for up to 10 minutes after logout, or after an owner hides a camera from the admin. Consider no-store, or a short max-age with must-revalidate.

uncovered.surface: dispatch_alerts and dispatch_live_alert sending evidence photos to Telegram (backend/app.py -> notifier.Notifier.send_photo)
uncovered.boundary: Per-camera admin_can_view and per-community event scope versus the single globally configured Telegram chat
uncovered.subsystem: Alert dispatch / derived copies of evidence
uncovered.reason: Every analyzed video's worst event (app.py:352-356) and every live event past the global cooldown (app.py:378-381) sends its evidence JPEG to one Telegram chat_id. This ignores the event's community, its owner, and whether the owner hid the camera from the admin. That chat is a derived copy of all communities' private evidence, readable by whoever is in the chat. The h4 alert-dispatch unit is scoped to abuse and quota (Business logic plus Resource exhaustion), not to this privacy and isolation question. The deployment fact of who reads the chat decides the impact.
